_comment: Every Vortex/fomod-installer source file this project ported or derived logic from (not called at runtime -- their behavior is hardcoded into lib/*.js). 'lastVerifiedCommit' is the SHA of the last commit that touched that exact file path, as of when we read it. check-vortex-source-drift.js re-queries GitHub for the CURRENT last-touching commit per file and flags any that no longer match, so an upstream Vortex behavior change doesn't silently desync our replicated logic. Re-run after any Vortex update, or periodically.

refs.whatWeDerived: flag application order (enableOption/disableOption via ConditionStateManager), per-option file collection via Union of selected options' Files

the 3-phase install order + hardcoded priority offsets (requiredInstallFiles=-10^9, selected-option files=0, conditionalFileInstalls=+10^9) and the ShouldUpdate destination-collision tie-break (higher priority wins; tie -> lexicographically greater source path wins)
conditionFlags accumulation semantics: SetFlagValue is a plain dictionary overwrite, so a later step's same-named flag replaces an earlier one; others persist
confirms Priority defaults/comparison semantics referenced by XmlScriptInstaller's tie-break (not directly ported, used to cross-check ShouldUpdate)

when a script IS found but its path isn't literally '...fomod\ModuleConfig.xml', the mod root falls back to ArchiveStructure.FindPathPrefix -- confirms our simpler 'always scan for fomod/ModuleConfig.xml anywhere' approach is a valid, simpler special case of the real logic

fomod-multi-config-selection (2026-09-15, 'mods it couldn't check show up instead of hiding'): GetRequirements()'s real rule for an archive with more than one fomod/ModuleConfig.xml -- `modFiles.FirstOrDefault(x => ScriptMatch(x, scriptFile))`, the FIRST match in the archive's own given file-list order wins, no depth/name sorting at all. Confirmed by reading the full method: UnsupportedException is thrown ONLY when the loop finds ZERO matches (`!HasFoundScriptType`) -- there is no ambiguous-case refusal anywhere in this path. findModRoot() used to throw on >1 match, which was never a real Vortex-side ambiguity (confirmed real: 'Better Skyrim Parties', two configs, Vortex installs it fine every time via this exact first-match rule) -- now takes archiveEntries[0]'s own match the same way, matching lib/sevenzip.js's own listArchive/parseSlt, which preserve 7z's own listing order verbatim (never re-sorted). REVISED 2026-09-16 ('pick a FOMOD installer in Vortex's exact file order'): 'the archive's own file-list order' was wrong -- see the walk.ts/InstallManager.ts entries just below for the real order. Also derived ScriptMatch's own exact match rule from this same file/commit: `Path.GetFileName(filePath).Contains(scriptFile, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && Path.GetFileName(Path.GetDirectoryName(filePath))?.Contains(FomodRoot, ...) == true` (scriptFile='ModuleConfig.xml', FomodRoot='fomod') -- a CONTAINS match on both the filename and the immediate parent folder's own bare name, not an exact 'fomod\ModuleConfig.xml' match. Checked empirically before widening lib/mod-root.js's own regex to this: a read-only pass over every real mod across all 22 of the director's real collections (4,362 mods) found 0 cases where the wider rule changes which file wins -- it only ever adds backup/versioned copies of an already-real config in the same folder, which always lose anyway (a name that's the real filename plus a trailing suffix always sorts after the real filename alone).

vortex-walk-order (2026-09-16, 'pick a FOMOD installer in Vortex's exact file order'): Vortex's own real file-list order for FOMOD/install-file resolution is NOT the archive's own internal listing order (7z's -slt order) -- Vortex extracts the archive to a temp folder first, then WALKS that real on-disk folder to build its file list (see the InstallManager.ts entry just below). walk()'s own real algorithm, read directly: `fs.readdirAsync(target)` for one directory, then EVERY direct child (file or subfolder, as a bare path) is added to the list in that readdir order via a synchronous `statResults.forEach` pass (confirmed: the callback's own list-push happens before `walkSubDirs()` is even invoked), THEN each subfolder is recursed into ONE AT A TIME in that same readdir order -- each subfolder's entire subtree finishes (recursively, by the same rule) before the next sibling subfolder even starts. Net effect: two paths that diverge at a shared ancestor are ordered by whichever diverging SIBLING sorts first there, regardless of nesting depth. lib/vortex-file-order.js's `sortByVortexWalkOrder` ports this ordering (as a pure function over already-known archive-entry paths, since this project never actually extracts-then-walks a real temp folder the way Vortex does) plus an NTFS-collation approximation (uppercase-then-ordinal string comparison) for the underlying readdir() order itself -- see that file's own header comment for why this is a documented approximation, not a byte-for-byte NTFS driver reimplementation.

confirms buildFileList(basePath) (~line 254, called from the real install path at ~line 1131) is what actually calls walk.ts's own walk() to build the 'modFiles' list ModFormatManager.cs's GetRequirements()/ScriptMatch iterate over -- `fileList.push(relPath)` (or `relPath + path.sep` for a directory) happens directly inside walk()'s own per-entry callback, confirming the callback's list-push really is synchronous within each directory's own readdir pass (not deferred), which is the load-bearing assumption behind lib/vortex-file-order.js's own 'batch siblings before recursion' ordering model.

confirms Install() actually calls GetRequirements() and takes ITS OWN FirstOrDefault() of the returned list (`new List<string>(GetRequirements(...)).FirstOrDefault()`) as the one real scriptFilePath used for the rest of the install -- a second, redundant 'first wins' layered on top of GetRequirements' own, not a different selection rule at a different stage.

the FindPathPrefix(fileList, expressions) algorithm itself: scan the file list in order, first path matching any stop-pattern regex, prefix = everything before the match. This is the core algorithm ported (not just referenced) into findPathPrefix() in simple-installer.js

the exact skyrimse stopPatterns list (uniPatterns + gamebryoPatterns + ['skse']), hardcoded verbatim as SKYRIMSE_STOP_PATTERNS/GAMEBRYO_TOP_LEVEL. THE single highest-risk drift point: if Vortex adds/removes a recognized top-level folder name or changes the pattern-building logic for skyrimse, our hardcoded list goes stale silently.

refs.derivedInto: extract-mod.js (choice of FOMOD vs simple path)
refs.whatWeDerived: confirms a non-FOMOD archive is handled by the SAME native installer in 'Basic' mode (isBasic=true), not a wholly separate code path -- justifies reusing the same stopPatterns mechanism for simple archives

confirms getStopPatterns(gameId, ...) is passed straight through to the native installer for both FOMOD and Basic mode -- no separate pluginPath-based second stripping pass observed in this file, which is why simple-installer.js does NOT do extra 'Data\' stripping

confirms Vortex's OWN update-checking logic (updateState()) reads attributes.version + attributes.fileId as the authoritative 'what's currently installed' fields -- NOT modVersion (doesn't appear in this logic at all) and NOT isPrimary. Grounded a real live experiment: after manually switching a mod's installed version in Vortex, attributes.version updated correctly but attributes.modVersion stayed stale at the old value -- this file is why we trust version/fileId and ignore modVersion when cross-referencing a mod's other installed versions.

ICommonModAttributes confirms version and modVersion are two genuinely separate, independently-settable fields (not a typo/duplicate) -- explains why they can diverge after a manual version switch. isPrimary is listed under 'Special mod types and flags', not the version/update section -- consistent with it being a Nexus 'main file' designation, not a local Vortex install-state concept, which is why we don't use it to determine what Vortex would deploy.

generateCollectionMap(): the real algorithm behind Vortex's own '+N collections' badge on the Mods page. Prefers rule.reference.id (a direct live-modKey link), falls back to findModByRef content-identity matching for a rule with no such id. CONFIRMED LIVE this session that rule.reference.id is NEVER populated for real collection-sourced rules -- only the fallback path is actually exercised for this project's data, which is why scanAllCollections mirrors findModByRef/testModReference below, not this file's primary path. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: generateCollectionMap moved out of collections/index.ts into collections/util/collectionsByMod.ts; same rule (rule.reference.id first, else findModByRef), so this entry now points at the new file.]
confirms the real fallback path when rule.reference.id is absent: delegates to testModReference (testRef) for content-identity matching, tried against every currently-installed mod.

testRef()'s real matching precedence: a tag MISMATCH is not immediately fatal if a stricter identifying marker (fileMD5, then repo.modId+repo.fileId) is present -- it falls through instead of refusing. Directly explains a real, confirmed-live finding: the identical file had a DIFFERENT rule.reference.tag value in each of 3 collections referencing it (tag is a deterministic-but-PER-COLLECTION value, not a stable cross-collection identity key -- see deterministicReferenceTag.ts, not separately pinned here). ruleIdentityKeys() deliberately matches by fileMD5 then repo.modId+fileId only, never tag, mirroring this real precedence rather than the naive assumption that a matching tag would be reliable. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: upstream only added a perf index (referenceIndex/rulesByReference); testRef() precedence unchanged. Vortex now also matches a tag against mod.referenceTags (several tags per mod); we never match on tag, so no change.]

script-extender-installer (2026-09-15, 'Rebuild Missing Files says Skyrim Script Extender is missing 536 files that are all there'): Vortex runs a SEPARATE, higher-priority installer (registerInstaller('script-extender-installer', 10, ...) -- same priority as the real-FOMOD installer, ahead of the generic Basic-mode fallback at 100) for any archive containing a known script-extender loader exe. Its real rule: find the loader exe (`files.find(basename === scriptExtExe)`), then `idx = scriptExtender.indexOf(path.basename(scriptExtender))`, `rootPath = path.dirname(scriptExtender)`, keep only files where `file.indexOf(rootPath) !== -1`, and set every kept file's destination to `file.substr(idx)` -- a single fixed-length prefix cut applied uniformly, NOT the generic stopPatterns/FindPathPrefix mechanism simple-installer.js already ports. Confirmed real: SKSE64's own archive nests a literal 'Data\' folder one level under its own top wrapper ('skse64_2_02_06\Data\Scripts\...', 'skse64_2_02_06\src\...', 'skse64_2_02_06\skse64_loader.exe') -- simple-installer.js's own stopPatterns mistook the nested 'Scripts' folder for an ordinary data-type mod's swallowable 'Data\' wrapper, stripping too much for src files and too little for Data files. Verified against the real archive + real staging folder: 536/536 files match exactly.

supportData's own scriptExtExe field per game -- the fixed loader-executable-name list this project's SCRIPT_EXTENDER_LOADER_EXES hardcodes verbatim: skse64_loader.exe (skyrimse, the one this project targets/verifies), skse_loader.exe (skyrim/LE), sksevr_loader.exe (skyrimvr), f4se_loader.exe (fallout4). Confirms the real algorithm is game-agnostic, keyed only on the loader's own basename.

confirms collection.json's own recorded `details.type: "dinput"` for a script-extender mod does NOT mean modtype-dinput's own dinput8.dll-seeking installer produced its file layout -- installScriptExtender() (script-extender-installer, priority 10, tried first) pushes `{type: 'setmodtype', value: 'dinput'}` itself, purely to set the DEPLOY TARGET (game root, mergeMods:true) after installing with its own, different file-layout rule. modtype-dinput's own install() (path.relative(basePath, filePath) against the folder containing dinput8.dll) never ran for SKSE at all -- SKSE ships no dinput8.dll.

confirms GHOST_EXT = '.ghost' is a real, Vortex-defined constant (gamebryo-plugin-management extension) -- the mechanism is specifically plugin (ESP/ESM/ESL) ghosting, not a generic deployment feature for arbitrary file types. Added AFTER the fix already shipped (the original fix was based on real observed on-disk behavior, not a source read) -- backfilled per this project's own standing practice of verifying against real Vortex source before/after implementing logic that mirrors it. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: file only moved into the renderer (gamebryo_plugin_management/statics.ts); GHOST_EXT is still ".ghost".]

toPluginId(fileName) = path.basename(fileName.toLowerCase(), GHOST_EXT) -- Vortex's own real logic for recovering a ghosted file's base identity: lowercase, then strip the literal '.ghost' suffix. Confirms stripGhostPairs()'s case-insensitive suffix-matching approach (match a '.ghost'-suffixed name in current staging against its stripped counterpart in the fresh archive extraction) is the same normalization Vortex itself uses, not an invented convention. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: file moved into the renderer; it is now path.basename(unghost(fileName)).toLowerCase() with unghost() in util/ghost.ts stripping a ".ghost" extension compared case-insensitively. Same result as before for our purposes: our case-insensitive suffix strip in stripGhostPairs() matches it.]

makeCollectionId(baseId) = 'vortex_collection_' + baseId -- confirms the 'vortex_collection_<id>' staging-folder naming convention this project uses to distinguish a Workshop-tab-only collection (never installed, or the Workshop copy only) from a real archive-installed one is Vortex's OWN real naming function, not an inferred/guessed pattern. Backfilled after the fact (the distinction was originally confirmed via live real-install observation, not a source read) per this project's standing practice of verifying against real Vortex source.

Vortex's own real 'download this exact modId+fileId from Nexus' trigger: build an nxm://<domain>/mods/<modId>/files/<fileId> URL and emit a 'start-download' event. Confirms the modId+fileId (not a search/guess) is the correct identity to resolve a specific file against, matching what this project's downloadModArchive() does via the direct REST call instead of the nxm:// protocol indirection (this project has no OS-level protocol handler to route through -- it calls the same underlying API endpoint directly). [Re-verified 2026-10-23: upstream change was only the event payload (mod_uid replaces mod_id/mod_name); the nxm://<domain>/mods/<modId>/files/<fileId> URL and start-download emit are unchanged.]

downloadFile()'s own explicit Premium-only gate for direct/automated downloads: 'nexusmods can't let users download files directly from client, without showing ads' -- a non-Premium account is refused client-side, by design, to protect Nexus's ad-supported revenue model for free users. This project's checkPremiumStatus() + upfront Premium check before any download attempt mirrors this exact policy rather than working around it -- a non-Premium account gets the same refusal Vortex's own client would give, with no attempt to route around Nexus's ad model. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: the Premium gate is unchanged, except it now first refreshes the cached membership before refusing (a plan bought on the website is picked up). Upstream also added rate-limit (429) handling in nexus_integration/rateLimit.ts.]

getDownloadURLs()'s real endpoint shape: GET /v1/games/{gameId}/mods/{modId}/files/{fileId}/download_link.json, no key/expires needed for Premium accounts (those are only for the free-user nxm-link-click flow this project does not implement). Response is an array of {URI,...} (or a single object) -- resolveDownloadLink() handles both shapes, matching this library's own res.download_links ?? [res.download_link] fallback. [Re-verified 2026-10-23: upstream changes were per-request header copies and rate-limit reading; the download_link.json endpoint shape is unchanged.]

preselectOptions(InstallStep): an option auto-selects when its resolved type is Required, or Recommended AND there's no preset to replay (!m_Preset.HasValue), or a preset name match, or the group is SelectAll. A SelectExactlyOne/SelectAtMostOne group with more than one option resolving Recommended repeatedly clears-then-selects, so the LAST qualifying option in document order ends up selected -- approximated client-side as 'take the last forced index'. A SelectExactlyOne group with nothing selected after all of the above falls back to its own first option (setFirst).

ResolveOptionType(): iterate a typeDescriptor's patterns in document order, return the FIRST pattern whose condition is fulfilled; fall back to DefaultType if none match. Matches fomodResolveType() exactly -- unchanged by this task, only the condition evaluation one level below it needed fixing.

GetIsFulfilled(): booAllFulfilled starts true for And / false for Or, then accumulates via &=/|= over each child condition. An EMPTY child list therefore returns the operator's own starting value -- true for And, FALSE for Or -- not vacuously true regardless of operator (this project's own prior bug, fixed here: native Array.prototype.every()/some() already give exactly this per-operator behavior on an empty array, with no length check needed).

fileDependency's real Active/Inactive/Missing semantics: Active -> coreDelegates.plugin.IsActive(path); Inactive -> IsPresent(path) && !IsActive(path); Missing -> !IsPresent(path). Ported into fomodFileDependencyMatches() using lib/missing-masters-scan.js's own scanDataFolder (Present)/computeActiveSet (Active) as the IsPresent/IsActive equivalents.

Confirms gameDependency/fommDependency/foseDependency/skseDependency/nvseDependency/f4seDependency are all a simple installedVersion >= MinimumVersion check against a live game-version-extender source Vortex's own delegates supply. This project has no such live source (no game-version-extender reader at all) -- these are parsed structurally for completeness but deliberately evaluated as always-satisfied, a disclosed, narrow limitation rather than a guessed comparison.

compositeDependency's real dependencyTypesGroup: fileDependency/flagDependency/gameDependency/fommDependency/foseDependency/skseDependency/nvseDependency/f4seDependency, AND a nested <dependencies> of type compositeDependency itself (maxOccurs unbounded, any mix, any order) -- confirms nested And/Or composites are a real, schema-legal FOMOD feature, not a speculative extension.

IsActive/IsPresent are case-insensitive membership checks against GetAll(true)/GetAll(false), which call back into Vortex's own getAllPlugins(activeOnly) -- confirms fileDependency resolution is answered entirely from Vortex's tracked PLUGIN list, never a generic file-on-disk check.

getAllPlugins(activeOnly): reads state.session.plugins.pluginList (mods with .esp/.esm/.esl files only), filtered by isPluginEnabled() when activeOnly. Confirms a fileDependency naming anything other than a real plugin file can NEVER resolve Active/Inactive in real Vortex -- it always resolves Missing, since it can never appear in this plugin-only tracked list. This is the source-grounded answer to 'what does Active mean for a non-plugin file', not a guess.
